description:
Programme or Project Overview

Maastricht University invites applications for a PhD candidate in spatial multi-omics and single-cell analysis of human diseases, with a start in January 2027. Spatial transcriptomics and related multi-omics technologies make it possible to map gene expression, chromatin state and protein levels within intact tissue, revealing how disease processes unfold across cell types and tissue niches. The doctoral project applies these technologies to human disease samples, building integrated single-cell and spatial atlases that connect molecular architecture to pathology.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral appointment under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement within Maastricht University's bioinformatics and molecular biology research environment. The doctoral candidate will process tissue samples, generate and analyse spatial and single-cell datasets, and develop computational workflows that integrate modalities, collaborating closely with pathologists and clinician-scientists. Maastricht's teaching-hospital setting provides direct access to well-annotated clinical material.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in biomedical sciences, molecular biology, bioinformatics or a related field, with an interest in genomics technologies and data analysis. Programming skills (Python or R) and familiarity with sequencing data are advantages; wet-lab and computational profiles are both welcome. Applications are submitted through Maastricht University's recruitment portal with a CV, transcripts, references and a motivation letter.

Highlights

  • PhD in spatial multi-omics with start January 2027
  • Single-cell and spatial profiling of human disease tissue
  • Integrated atlases linking molecules to pathology
  • Salaried employment under the CAO-NU agreement
  • Close collaboration with pathologists and clinician-scientists
  • Well-annotated clinical samples from an academic hospital
